audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Irelia "he/his" in tldr, phases, both do's and the don'ts, and Level 3, Levels 4-5, First item and 2+ items are marked Irelia while carrying Akshan-favoured boilerplate.
audit.why: Irelia is female. The stage sides are correct — the lane really does turn at 3 when Flawless Duet arrives — but the stage text argued the opposite of the side it sat on.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed and the four contradicted stages now name their own mechanic: Flawless Duet at 3, its 16s cooldown across 4-5, Defiant Dance's physical reduction at first item, and Bladesurge resets at two.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vanguard's Edge appears nowhere on the page in either layer, and no cooldown is given for anything.
audit.why: Vanguard's Edge (125/105/85) leaves a blade wall that damages and slows anyone walking through it. Against a champion whose only escape is a terrain grapple, a wall dropped behind you is the thing that turns a survivable trade into a death — and it was never mentioned. Flawless Duet's 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s is likewise the number the entire lane schedules around.
audit.corrected: Flawless Duet's 16s rank-1 cooldown is stated in the win condition, the 4-5 stage, the cooldown block, the do's and the interactions report, and Vanguard's Edge's retreat-cutting wall is written into the late text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ionian Fervor is described as resistance shred in five strings — "stacked passive shred melts your resists", "once her passive stacks shred your resists", "stacked passive shred eats your low base durability". Defiant Dance is described only as a generic "damage block".
audit.why: Ionian Fervor shreds nothing. Riot's description: striking enemies with spells gives her stacking bonus attack speed, and at maximum stacks bonus on-hit damage. Building armour against her therefore still works, which is the opposite of what the page implies. Defiant Dance is more specific than described too — she "takes reduced PHYSICAL damage during the charge", and every point of Akshan's damage is physical, so it is a full counter to your entire kit rather than a partial one.
audit.corrected: All five strings now describe Ionian Fervor as stacking attack speed and on-hit, and Defiant Dance is stated as physical-specific reduction against an all-physical kit.

edits.before: She owns the late game outright. Her Q resets off your wave for permanent gap-close, her E two-mark stun locks you out of Heroic Swing every time, and her W block plus stacked passive shred chew through your squishy lethality frame while you can't burst her down anymore. Your only path is converting an early-to-mid lead into towers and map pressure before her items land — splitpushing into her once she scales is suicide. If the game goes long, stop dueling her: group and fire R from range to pick her squishier teammates instead of brawling the Irelia.
edits.after: She owns the late game outright. Her Q resets off your wave for permanent gap-close, her E two-mark stun locks you out of Heroic Swing every time, and Defiant Dance cuts your all-physical damage while Ionian Fervor stacks her attack speed. Worse, Vanguard's Edge leaves a blade wall that cuts your retreat, so the ground you swung toward may not be open. Your only path is converting an early-to-mid lead into towers before her items land — splitpushing into her once she scales is suicide. If it goes long, stop dueling her: group and fire R from range at her squishier teammates.

notes: Vanguard's Edge creates a wall of blades. Whether Heroic Swing can grapple that wall as terrain is not answerable from Riot's data, so nothing was written either way — but it is worth confirming, because if it can, her ultimate accidentally hands you an escape anchor in open lane, and if it cannot, the current 'cuts your retreat' framing is the whole story.
